answer: Before the storm season the shelter master cuts snow blocks to gauge and inspects every shelter, writing the repairs in the construction log. A relic shelter piled up in an hour fails the log: at the lagoon of the wall the blocks must measure as the gauge demands, and a hurried shelter collapses on its sleepers. Forging the log means building shelters for three storms, inspecting 90 of them and paying 7,800, while the echo signature in the log is read before every blizzard, so a shelter whose blocks were never gauged is barred to all.
